query: Why do some agents have longer resolution times?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Directly operationalizes the query's target metric, giving the core axis for analysis. However, groundedness is compromised: many negative values (e.g. -4.29, -106.7) are not derivable from valid timestamps, and the row samples only show closed_at/sys_updated_on with no opened_at present, so computed values cannot be verified and negatives contradict a sensible reading.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: A clean numeric encoding of the existing priority column, useful for correlating priority with resolution time. Largely redundant with an original column, but still adds modeling leverage. Values are a faithful mapping of the source.

per_column.name: agent_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Highly relevant to 'why some agents have longer resolution times' -- provides a per-agent aggregate axis. Derivable from the table via grouping on assigned_to, though it inherits the questionable resolution_hours base and the '750' spike/'0' values suggest some aggregation artifacts.

per_column.name: agent_concurrent_load
per_column.rationale: A genuinely new explanatory axis (workload) that plausibly explains slower resolution -- strong analytical value. Computable from overlapping open intervals per agent, but this depends on opened_at/closed_at which are not visible in samples, so only partially verifiable.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Adds a category-level benchmark useful for separating agent effects from case-type effects. Derivable by grouping on the existing category column, though it inherits the resolution_hours reliability issues.

per_column.name: is_self_closed
per_column.rationale: A meaningful binary flag (whether closed_by equals assigned_to/caller) that could correlate with resolution behaviour. Derivable by comparing closed_by with other person fields; a reasonable categorisation, though the samples don't fully expose the compared fields.

judge.rationale: The added columns are well-aimed at the query: they supply the core resolution-time metric plus multiple distinct explanatory axes (agent averages, concurrent workload, category benchmark, self-closed flag, priority encoding), giving real leverage to explain why some agents are slower. The main weakness is groundedness of resolution_hours: numerous negative values are not a sound reading of timestamps, and since resolution_hours feeds the agent/category averages, that unreliability propagates. Values are otherwise consistent with grouping/encoding of existing columns.
